evidence: Repeating the cycle grows smooth, continuous, stoichiometric films of thicknesses adjustable from angstroms to >100 nm, as demonstrated by spectroscopic ellipsometry, XRR, AFM, UV–vis and Raman spectroscopy, XPS, and TEM. The prompt oxidation of the ALD film is observed in a transmission electron microscopy (TEM) experiment. The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) radial integrated intensity reveals order on a very short length scale. The chemical identity (elemental composition) of this film can only be determined after encapsulation with a protective layer. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopic microanalysis performed of a ZnS-capped HfS2 ALD coating yields an atomic composition. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis: Figure 6 presents the ZnS-capped film. The S 2p doublet at 161.5 and 162.7  eV attributed to ZnS is now complemented by an additional contribution from HfS2, at lower energies, 161.1 and 162.3 eV. Raman spectroscopy is a versatile method to determine structural properties such as thickness, crystallographic structure, and the presence of defects in thin layered materials. The Raman spectrum recorded of a HfS2 coating upon excitation at 532 nm is presented. The optical absorption spectra were measured with an ultraviolet-visible spectrophotometer. X-ray reflectometry measurements were performed. Secondary electron microscope (SEM) images were acquired. Atomic force microscope (AFM) imaging was carried out. IRAS Measurements: The measurements were performed in an UHV setup. The thickness of the deposited HfS2 layers was determined on Si (100) wafers with a spectroscopic ellipsometer. Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) was measured. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectra were recorded. Raman spectrum of the thin film was measured in ambient conditions. The optical absorption spectra were measured with an ultraviolet-visible spectrophotometer. X-ray reflectometry measurements were performed. Secondary electron microscope (SEM) images were acquired. Atomic force microscope (AFM) imaging was carried out.
